summary: A time capsule buried in 1953 was unearthed in Midbury on September 21, 2023, revealing kitchenware and handwritten recipes. The find has sparked interest from historians, chefs, and educators, and is inspiring community dinners, festivals, farm-to-table efforts, and similar discoveries elsewhere in the region. The note frames the artifacts as a link between past and present culinary heritage.
one_line: A 1953 time capsule of recipes and kitchenware unearthed in Midbury in 2023 is reviving local culinary heritage through dinners, education, and festivals.
key_facts: A rusted metal time capsule was unearthed on September 21, 2023, beneath the old oak tree in the central square of Midbury; it had been buried in 1953.
The capsule contained a cast iron skillet, an array of wooden spoons, a hand-cranked egg beater, and a ceramic mixing bowl, all showing marks of frequent use.
Handwritten recipes included 'Grandma Eileen's Famous Apple Pie' and 'Uncle Thom's Cornbread,' written on yellowing paper and preserved in plastic sleeves.
Grandma Eileen's apple pie recipe names apple varieties local to Midbury that are now scarce, and involves hand-peeling and slicing apples and making dough from scratch.

Food historian Martha Simms said recipes passed down through generations tell the story of a region's agriculture, economic conditions, and immigrant influences, calling the skillet 'a vessel of heritage.'
Local chef and food writer Susan Rodriguez said recipes are 'instruction sets for cultural expression.'
Educator Johnathan Greene said the items can be an essential educational resource for exploring history through food.
Culinary arts programs are eager to reintroduce the historical cooking methods and dishes into their curriculum.
Local chefs, including Susan Rodriguez, plan a series of community dinners using the same methods and, where possible, the same locally sourced ingredients as the recipes.
Rodriguez is creating a modern twist on Uncle Thom's Cornbread using heirloom corn and contemporary flavors.
Midbury is planning annual festivals celebrating its heritage with traditional foods, and farm-to-table initiatives are growing.
In nearby Eastwood, a 1968 time capsule revealed old canning jars with preserved fruits and a vintage pie safe with intricate patterns, pointing to regional variations in preservation and baking.
